neighbours.label: 'as' introducing a scientific role for an organism or measure ('useful as indicator species', 'serve as indicators')
fire: Frogs are often used as indicator species for wetland health.
Mosses can serve as bioindicators of heavy-metal pollution.
Mayfly larvae act as sensitive indicators of clean streams.
Coral cover is widely used as a measure of reef condition.
Bees are valuable as sentinels of pesticide exposure in farmland.
Tree rings serve as a record of past rainfall in the region.
Earthworms function as indicators of healthy agricultural soil.
Blood lactate is used as a marker of exercise intensity.
quiet: Frogs are often found near ponds and slow-moving streams.
Mosses can grow on rocks, roofs and the bark of old trees.
Mayfly larvae live for months on the bottoms of clean streams.
Coral reefs are home to thousands of species of fish.
Bees visit many flowers in farmland during the summer months.
Tree rings form each year as the trunk grows wider.
Earthworms dig tunnels through agricultural soil after rain.
Blood lactate rises sharply during hard exercise sessions.

notes: Top peak 'useful as indicator species' (113); other peaks are ' and'/' National'/' Phys' in scientific text. Probe: 'serve as indicators' 0.45, 'useful as indicator' 0.26, other science 0.06-0.13.
